opportunities.objective: The joint force needs inexpensive and capable aerial Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) solutions to provide decision and targeting quality data across land, littoral, and maritime environments. Current ISR solutions are often tethered to vulnerable airfields and infrastructure, have large manning requirements, and are too expensive to widely proliferate. Additionally, the exquisite nature, low manufacturing throughput, and high cost of legacy systems hinders their employment in contested areas – the very areas they are often most needed. As such, the Department of War often struggles to meet its aggregate ISR demands in support of the joint force. The Department of War (DoW) seeks both medium and long-endurance Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) or other platforms that can collect and transmit multi-intelligence (multi-int) sensor data to support real-time operational and targeting decisions over expansive land, littoral, and maritime regions. opportunities.objective: The cost-exchange ratio for detecting and neutralizing asymmetric maritime and airborne threats in contested environments is heavily skewed in favor of the adversary. Today the Department of War (DoW) too often relies on exquisite, multi-million-dollar naval surface and aviation assets to counter these inexpensive threats. Low-cost, low-signature threats—including explosive Unmanned Surface Vessels (USVs), Group 1–3 Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS), attack helicopters, go-fast vessels, and low-flying aerial vectors—directly threaten surface-fleet operations. The current force packages lack sufficient persistent, distributed capability to search for, track, and defeat these threats at an economically sustainable cost. The Department of War Innovation Unit (DIU), in partnership with the Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager for Unmanned Systems (DRPM UxS), seeks mature, production-ready, maritime counter-air solutions through a multi-phase Prize Challenge under 10 U.S.C. § 4025 . For Sprint 2, DIU seeks integrated combinations of mature USVs and hard-kill counter-air effectors suitable for forward operational fielding within 120 days. Sprint 2 focuses specifically on detecting, tracking, and defeating hostile airborne threats in contested maritime environments.
